Canon EF 24-105mm f/4 L IS USM Lens for Canon EOS SLR Cameras The Canon 24-105mm f/4 L lens with Image Stabilization is a fantastic lens for those times when you just want to have one lens on the camera but you also want to have a lot of options with your focal range. The range on this lens takes you from a decent wide angle perspective to a mid-range telephoto without any light loss (the maximum aperture is constant throughout the zoom range) and image stabilization keeps focus problems due to hand shake well away.

Optical quality is excellent, as you would expect with an L lens, and autofocus is smooth and fast. Keep in mind on a camera with a cropped sensor (any Canon DSLR model other than the 5D and 1D models) the focal range is equivalent to @40-170mm - you lose a bit of the wide angle advantage, but you get more telephoto, so it depends which end of the focal range you value the most as to whether that is a disadvantage or not.
text_fidelity_b: Canon EF 24-105mm f/4 L IS USM Lens for Canon EOS SLR Cameras

Nomodo U Wireless Wearable Bluetooth Speaker, Rechargeable and Portable I ordered the 'Nomodo U Wireless Wearable Bluetooth Speaker, Rechargeable and Portable' for review and would like to share some of my thoughts and experiences.
First off, out of the box this Bluetooth Wireless Speaker not only looks interesting but it is beautiful. I say interesting because I have never had a Wireless Speaker like this, and I wonder where would I use it and would it be practical. Well after some time with this device I must first report that it really does sound amazing. The sound is clean and immersive. It is hard to describe the incredible sound sensation while wearing it. It is almost as if you have speakers floating on either side of your head (pointing directly to your ears) and it is nothing like I have experienced before but it is pretty cool. I have been trying to think of how this Speaker would actually fit into my life. It's not like you are wearing headphones that only you can hear. While wearing this speaker, everyone else around you can hear it too but it's just not as immersive as it is to you. It's hard to describe, but what I will say is that it really is an incredible experience. If the volume is down low you can still hear your surroundings yet when you crank it up, surprisingly your surrounding sounds seem to disappear. Personally I have decided that this would be best worn while alone in your home while doing simple household chores. Like doing dishes or folding laundry. The Nomodo U speaker stays put pretty well for the most part due to the rubber neck pad, yet if you are constantly bending over or doing anything where you are moving around a lot and twisting your head and body, it tends to need re adjusted. Sitting in bed listening to Music or listening to an audio book works really well with this device as long as you wont be disturbing your partner. As for watching movies, for me this really doesn't work. I can't find anywhere where it says what version of Bluetooth this is using but I don't think it is Bluetooth 5.0 unfortunately. There are noticeable sync issues and this just gets annoying. Speaking of the Bluetooth, it connects/pairs effortlessly to all of my devices and that is a bonus. I am disappointed however that it uses Micro USB (the cable is included btw) for charging. With this being a new device it should have USB Type C. I always have to mention this with any new devices. Call quality is acceptable. Those on the other end can hear you just fine, as long as you are not in a loud environment. This is pretty typical with most wireless headphones. Overall I do love this device and think it is a great value for what it is.
text_fidelity_b: Nomodo U Wireless Wearable Bluetooth Speaker, Rechargeable and Portable

text_fidelity_a:
Flip Ultra Video Camera - Black, 1 GB, 30 Minutes (1st Generation) This camcorder is a simple way for you to share videos with friends and family, make and share mini-movies, capture special moments, or film your next masterpiece for YouTube or Amazon.com.

Pros:
1. The "cool" factor is off the scale. Every time I showed it to somebody, they said "COOL!!!"

2. It uses two AA batteries that are easy to install. There's a latch at the bottom of the camera - one side has a picture of a closed lock, and the other has a picture of an open lock. It doesn't get simpler than that, does it? Push towards the open lock and slide off the panel on the front of the camera from just under the lens. After you put in the batteries, slide the panel back into place and push the latch back to the locked position. You're now ready to start filming.

3. There are very few buttons required to operate the camera. Turning it so that the side with the big red button is facing you, the on/off switch is on the right side of the camera. After powering up, the screen will light up with the Flip logo and then it will indicate that it's ready. At this stage you'll be looking at whatever's in front of you, with a time check at the bottom telling you how much video time you have left.

4. Filming is easy - just press the red button to start, and press it again to stop. The camera will save your creation, tell you how long it is and how much time you have left. You can zoom in and out by pressing the + and - signs on top of and below the red button. The microphone will pick up and record whatever's going on at the time.

5. Playback is a one button operation.

6. Deleting your mistakes is a one button operation.

7. You can scroll through your videos by using the arrow keys to the left and right of the red button.

8. Getting it on your computer is the easiest part. With the red button facing you, pull down on the latch on the left side, and - surprise!!! Out pops a USB arm which you then connect to your computer. Once you're linked up, the Flip Video software will show you the way home. (It takes a while to pop up) Choose the option to view your videos, and agree to the terms and conditions, and then the "Muvee Video Mixing Software" begins loading. This is a one time installation. From there you can easily play, name, edit and share your videos.

9. You can also capture still shots from your videos, but you can't use these when making your movies with the software provided.

10. There is an option for making a movie, where you can arrange your edited videos, choose from a selection of six movie styles and music, or even add your own music. Choose your style, click on the "Make Mix" button, and the computer does the rest. If you're happy with the results, you can save the file.

11. The camera comes with a wrist strap, a velvet drawstring case, and also the necessary cables to connect it to your television for a bigger view. There's also a place to connect a tripod.

12. There is a "Help" feature included with the software.

Cons:
1. Being a simple "point and shoot" camera, the resolution isn't fantastic, but quite good enough for action shots. Forget detail close-ups such as words and logos - zooming in and out will just get you various degrees of blurry.

2. You'll need to be careful with background noise, as the microphone will pick up the sound of your fan or your stomach growling.

3. The video editing capability is limited to the length of the video you want to save, and the order you want to save it. There are no options for titles, fade ins or outs or any bells and whistles. If you're filming yourself giving a speech, you'll pretty much have to get it right in one complete take.

4. As with all videos, if your hands shake, you'll need to get a tripod, or you may make a lot of people seasick.

5. If you have big fingers, you may have some problems with the red button. Once your finger covers the area around the button, you'll have trouble starting and stopping the video. If you can't get it to work, you may have to use just a fingernail, because if you press anywhere other than dead center of the red button it won't start or stop.

Overall, this is a very good camcorder if used for the purpose for which it is intended. It isn't going to make you the next Stanley Kubrick, but it's a good start.

Amanda Richards, October 9, 2007
text_fidelity_b: Flip Ultra Video Camera - Black, 1 GB, 30 Minutes (1st Generation)

From the pictures you would think the front is all matte black, it is not. It's actually a very dark brown and the controls are a dark bronze, in shiny metal; closer to chrome aesthetic and looks far better with more tones than the photos would suggest. I'm actually happy I bought the darker color now seeing it. I tried to capture this on my pic, but it's too dark and still doesn't capture the wonderful appearance.

Plugging it in and turning it on was instantly satisfying, easy to use controls, no stiffness, good quality, lights work, radio is a deep amber or orange. Nice wood, looks and operates easily and great.

Tuning to a somewhat hard to get classical station locally was surprisingly easy and the signal came in loud and clear, unlike the other radios I've tried from Amazon. It felt like an old stereo where you didn't have to give it thought and was instinctive in the first 30 seconds without the difficulty and poor reception and static and crackling of tuning and volume controls or pops of turning it on nearly all cheap modern radios have now.

Bluetooth connected and performed seamlessly, perhaps a little softer than the radio but not horribly so. And the sound... On both radio and bluetooth the sound quality is superb; *just* enough bass without being muddy and the treble is good and clear. Bass in the voices and high pitches in the music, and very loud without screech or static at still low volume on the knob, with room-filling sound on FM and bluetooth.

This is the most pleasing product I've purchased from Amazon in a long time, especially in the radio category.

Update: After trying several others, I bought a second one! Like New $21. The only thing I notice is neither sits perfectly evenly, there's a slight wobble, even with all four feet pads. No biggie. Love the radio, excellent big sound, bass, but not muddy. Best radio on Amazon, and a true "table radio".
text_fidelity_b: Victrola Retro Wood Bluetooth FM/AM Radio with Rotary Dial, Espresso

text_fidelity_a:
Fujifilm Instax Mini 26 + Rainbow Film Bundle - Black A long time ago I had access to a Polaroid Instamatic camera. It was great - snap a picture, it spits out a sheet. Wait about 2 minutes and what you have is a printed photograph. Polaroid is gone now (though the name gets licensed over and over again), and with it went all of the film for the camera that made it so useful. This new camera by Fuji brings back some of the fun of instant photos, though it is by no means perfect and it suffers from some of the same issues the older Polaroid camera had.

The idea is very straightforward - point-and-shoot, and the camera ejects an exposure that will develop over a few moments and will be fully developed in approximately 2 minutes. This is great for social events and is a fun way to share candid shots. The camera is very lightweight and it is small too so it is easy to pack and carry with you.

There are a few issues with the camera, though, some of which are very much like the old Polaroids of days gone by. The images do come out a bit grainy and are definitely not high resolution. If you are looking for images with nice, clean edge detail and bright, vibrant colors, this is going to disappoint you. Also, the images are really small, a little bigger than a passport picture but not by very much. And finally, the film is relatively expensive, a pack of exposures coming with only 10 slides and costing about $0.60 per exposure.

On the plus side, the camera is very easy to use and the camera body itself is not very expensive at all.

There are trade-offs with this camera. On one hand, it is super convenient, it’s fun and it’s relatively inexpensive. However, exposure quality is mediocre, pictures are small and on a per-picture basis the exposures are somewhat expensive. To me, the fun factor weighs heavily in favor of this camera and offsets some of the negatives. For social gatherings and recreational events, this is a fun camera and will serve well. Do not expect to have high-end results, though.
text_fidelity_b: Fujifilm Instax Mini 26 + Rainbow Film Bundle - Black

Samsers Foldable Bluetooth Keyboard - Portable Wireless Keyboard with Stand Holder, Rechargeable Full Size Ultra Slim Folding Keyboard Compatible iOS Android Windows Smartphone Tablet & Laptop-Silver The Samsers Wireless Portable Folding Keyboard is only 1/2" thick when folded, and of course, half that when undfolded. It is quite thin and portable. It caught my attention because it supports pairing with up to 3 bluetooth devices simultaneously and with many of us having multiple devices (phone and tablet is quite normal), these devices are great for someone like me.

The clamshell design means that the keys are protected when closed. It also holds itself closed magnetically, and powers on my simply opening it. Pairing is easy: hold the function key and press one of the Q,W, or E keys to select one of the three bluetooth slots, then press the big "connection" button on the left bezel of the keyboard. This all seems pretty slick to me but I did have one concern with this keyboard's design and that is the hinge system. When the keyboard is open, it is quite easy to twist it with just a little bit of pressure. It means that I'm always extra careful when I'm taking it out of my bag.

In terms of functionality, the keys are a the same size as the ones on my laptop and has the same amount of travel as well, although they are a little bit louder than my laptop's keys when typing. I'm using this keyboard to type this review right now. What I found is that the keys are a little bit unresponsive. I keep missing letters every few words I type. Just in this last sentence, I had to go back about 5 times to correct missing letters. This defeats the purpose of purchasing a keyboard to type more quickly on a mobile device. Perhaps if you are normally heavy-handed when you type on a keyboard, you wouldn't face this issue.

Something that I wish this keyboard had is a touch pad. If this device can be both a keyboard and mouse, it would be much more useful.

Overall, the Samsers Wireless Portable Folding Keyboard is a good device but ultimately, it has a couple of shortcomings that keep it from being great.

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech G13 Programmable Gameboard with LCD Display Pros:
-Easily programmed.
-Multiple game memory.
-Many, many keys = many, many programming options.
-Digital readout looks good and lets you know exactly what download you are using without reopening Logitech window.

Cons:
-Flat palm positioning is not very comfortable for gaming (and can't be adjusted). My hand tends to cramp due to its bad ergonomics when playing FPS games more than an hour.
-Keypad ergonomics are badly thought out. Key rows are positioned bowing UPWARDS (away from your fingers) instead of downwards, making quick initiation of pinky and index finger keys more difficult.
-G13 is a bit large and can't easily be slid aside when not gaming (not a big deal to me, but somewhat inconvenient).
-Friends tell me that Razer and Logitech downloads interfere with one another, so if you have a Razer mouse or keyboard this may interfere with your use of either.
-Keys are a bit too close together without easily discernible gaps in between. This too often causes my thick fingers to strike 2 keys simultaneously.
-Overpriced for what it offers.

Overall:
Programming=excellent. Ergonomics=horrible.
For me, the keypad layout and palm rest do not work together. They look like they should, but they simply do not. The device concept is quite good, but the ergonomics make it just too difficult to consistently access and manipulate keys for real-time gaming. Very disappointing to me because with Logitech's years of experience in peripherals this should put Nostromo to shame---it simply doesn't because of the badly positioned keys and faulty wrist/palm rest ergonomics.

Follow-up:
-Down from 2 to only 1 Star, and it should be ZERO Stars. This thing is good only for a paperweight to remind me of my wasted time and wasted money.
-6 months down the road and, while gaming, each and every one of my gaming profiles (I have 3) will spontaneously reset to the default profile on their own or, even worse, all the G-keys become unresponsive.
-Sometimes on computer start-up the LCD screen lights up, but no profiles appear, not even default, and no keys respond.
-Sometimes on computer start-up the unit never powers on.
-Logitech's updates do not fix the problem(s). I've deleted the entire gaming software setup and performed reinstalls ad nauseum with no permanent positive result. What's even worse is this: it acts fine for a bit after a reinstall, so you think you've corrected it, then it starts screwing up ALL OVER AGAIN.
-BIOS adjustments do not fix the problems.
-USB ports and motherboard are completely functional throughout my gaming (I've tested/monitored them as I play) and they perform perfectly as the gamepad and/or its software crashes on its own.
-It's only 6 months old, and 2 keys are mechanically non-functional (G20 and the button below the joystick). My Belkin Nostromo n52 lasted for almost 8 YEARS of gaming with no problems whatsoever, and I was gaming three times as much back then. I'd grown used to the G13 so I was willing to overlook the buttons, or blame them on myself, and work around this issue, but when the software/electrical issues began occurring quite regularly I'd run out of patience.
-Forums addressing these (as well as other) issues have found no answers or solutions, only make-shift quick-fixes.
-Numerous forums also share the information that this is happening across a variety and multitude of different computer systems/set-ups.
-Many other owners, myself included, have had additional problems with the G13 when it is used after a computer has hibernated/slept, but we all learned to live with this as one of its quirks. We now see this as an indicator of its many issues.
-Many other owners have said that the problems began occurring after 3 or more months use (I suspect that in my case this took longer as it is only occasionally used for gaming).
-Logitech customer support has denied any fault in these matters and still maintains that their pruduct and programming is NOT the cause of any of these problems, so their help line has been useless. Meanwhile, the price plummets as word spreads.
-Only thing that works for any of us is to constantly disconnect gamepad from its current USB port, reconnect it, and computer may recognize it...but this does NOT always work...sometimes requires reboot as well...and sometimes this doesn't work either...so gamepad is inoperative until it decides to come back on a reconnection or restart. This is a band-aid at best. I refuse to do this to my system over and over.

This thing is getting returned. I advise you to save your money and time by buying some other manufacturer's product.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech G13 Programmable Gameboard with LCD Display

Creative Technology Speaker - for Portable use - USB This speaker set sounds great for its size. The sound is loud and clear, but also full in the way you would expect stereo sound to be. It is also small enough to travel fairly easily, although it is not the smallest on the market. This is capable of getting louder than you'll ever be able to use in a hotel room, but suitable for an apartment; there are plenty of options out there in the form of travel speakers.

The built in mic is obviously a significant factor, and it works great compared to my laptop mic. I do like the fact that it gets its power and signal over one cable, but sometimes I think I'm going to run out of USB ports since I use them regularly to charge my phones and other devices. And I was also expecting bluetooth after seeing the ads for the other models. But who cares about bluetooth when you still need power?-smaller speakers don't need an external power source.

This is a good product and I'm certain to use it, especially when travelling for long enough that I want to set up more of a "home" that includes music. It is sort of another take on what is already a niche product, however, and although I do think it's one of the better styles on the market, it's still not the end all of small speakers, nor does it make dramatic improvements over what is already available. It's great at packing full sound into something very portable, and it eliminates one cable if you use USB, but then you use up another USB port. I'd love to see it either fully wireless with included battery or also include a webcam to preclude the need for other accessories. Yes, I know these things would up the cost, but it would make a truly remarkable product.

I also like how the invisible button panel appears when powered on, but not how you can't completely turn it off without removing the power source. The speaker looks good and I like how all sides are covered in speaker screen material, but I worry I could easily stick my finger through a cone.

A quality product that is great if it closely fits your needs.
text_fidelity_b: Creative Technology Speaker - for Portable use - USB

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Versa Smart Watch, Peach/Rose Gold Aluminium, One Size (S & L Bands Included), Heart Rate Monitor I got the FitBit Versa because I wanted to try a smart watch without having to buy an expensive Apple Watch. The FitBit is comfortable to wear and looks nice. I like that it tracks my heart rate and steps. What I really wanted was to see my notifications on my watch. This watch allows you to see your notifications and will even vibrate to remind you of events on your phone calendar. It is lacking in a couple areas. One— you can see your notifications but you cannot interact with them at all. It also only shows text, so if someone texts you a gif or emoji it shows up as a blank message. It also doesn’t consistently give me my notifications, but that could be a phone setting issue. Second— the available apps are limited. You can play music, but only from a couple platforms. You cannot play Amazon music, audible, Scribd, podcaster... Also, the fertility tracking app for FitBit is ridiculously limiting. It is possibly the worst tracking I have ever seen. Since that is in the realm of health, I think it should be a lot better. It is effectively unusable.
So while this is a cheaper option than others and has heart rate tracking and such, there are still some limitations. It is waterproof— so I can wear it in the pool. Battery lasts about 3 days on one charge. And you can customize the watch face to your liking.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Versa Smart Watch, Peach/Rose Gold Aluminium, One Size (S & L Bands Included), Heart Rate Monitor

text_fidelity_a:
Ritz Gear 64GB High-Speed SDXC UHS-II SD Card, C10, U3, V90, Full-HD & 8K Memory Card for DSLR, Cinema-Quality Video Cameras This is a great card if you have a reader and/or camera compatible with the newer UHS-II format. I shoot a lot of 4k video on Sony cameras, so I very much appreciate being able to copy lots of high bitrate footage after a shoot VERY quickly, which is exactly what this does!
You can always spot the UHS-II cards by their extra pins on the back. With a reader that can utilize them, I found this card performed pretty excellent in my benchmarks! 257MB/s read and a whopping 248MB/s write! That's incredible speed for write, I wasn't expecting it. On my other cards, UHS-II boosted the read times to similar proportions but write was similar to regular U3 class SDXC cards. That this Ritz card can produce similar write times as the boosted read is pretty incredible! This might be my new favorite media.
text_fidelity_b: Ritz Gear 64GB High-Speed SDXC UHS-II SD Card, C10, U3, V90, Full-HD & 8K Memory Card for DSLR, Cinema-Quality Video Cameras

text_fidelity_a:
Creative Technology Speaker - Wireless - Bluetooth - USB, Bluetooth This is the second "Creative" brand wireless bluetooth speaker with microphone, and so far, the sound quality has not been very good. The first, "Creative Sound BlasterAxx SBX10 Wireless Bluetooth Speaker with Microphone" was $127.04 (list price $149.99), and this one currently has a list price of $199.99. I cannot hear any discernable difference in sound quality, though this speaker is larger than the other. They are both OK for being usb powered, but there are better-sounding products out there for the same price if you are willing to sacrifice the speaker option.

I ran the same tests on this speaker as the other and got identical results:

This one gets a mixed review for the overall sound quality, but it does have some features that make it very useful. I will be reviewing its various features individually so you can better assess if this meets your needs or not. I used a decibel measuring app on my phone to determine when the speakers began to distort some of what I played.

Playing audio with Bluetooth or via USB with a computer:
-There is no noticeable difference with playback using Bluetooth versus USB connection to a computer, and it has a Very long range (I walked about 25ft away and it was still doing fine)

AUDIO

75 DECIBELS AND UNDER:
Almost all audio was fine: clear, undistorted, and with pretty good clarity (don't expect GREAT quality or clarity. Just Good.) Some types of music fared poorly even at this relatively soft volume. I used "Fortuna from Carmina Burana" to test the system's limits. (YouTube the piece if you want to know which song I refer to--you'll recognize it immediately) The chorus of singers sounded distorted. At higher volumes, even as lot as 85db, it was awful. Other types of music were fine (orchestra music, pop, hip hop, electronica), but sometimes the treble was a bit fuzzy.

75-85 DECIBELS:
This is the maximum volume the speakers can reach with the USB connection, so it can get loud enough for a small-medium party, but not Very loud.
It's hit and miss here. The treble and bass have some problems, especially treble. The clarity diminishes and any nuances in your music will generally get a bit lost or muffled. Choral music, music with higher pitched percussive elements, and some types of rock and orchestra music don't sound very good.

PHONE CALLS:
The voice of the person you are calling sounds a bit muffled--definitely not as good as headphones or the phone, but about on par with other Bluetooth systems I've tried.

The voice of the speaker (i.e. You) is actually clear! This part gets a solid review. With my built-in car Bluetooth system, as well as detachable ones I've reviewed, usually the person you are calling has trouble hearing you and can experience interference. Maybe that is because it is in the car and there's road noise, but in any case, the fact this one does, actually, sound clear to the recipient of your phone call is a BIG plus.

Overall, this is a good product when you compare it to other desktop laptop speakers. If you are comparing it to products specifically meant for enjoying audio, however, I would recommend the Pioneer Electronics Audition Series for a relatively inexpensive but high quality experience, or Bose if you are looking for something higher-end. The price of the Pioneer product is almost the same, and while it doesn't have Bluetooth unless you buy the attachment separately (about $70) and it only docks with the older iPhone and iPods, the sound quality of that one is stunning. If you want extra features like FREE Bluetooth and speakerphone capability, this one is ok for the price. Not great. Just ok.

Because this is basically the same as the "Creative Sound BlasterAxx SBX10 Wireless Bluetooth Speaker with Microphone", and the other is about $70 cheaper, I would recommend getting the SBX10 and saving your money. They are basically the same thing, so either pay more and get better sound quality with another product entirely, or pay less for the same thing.
text_fidelity_b: Creative Technology Speaker - Wireless - Bluetooth - USB, Bluetooth

text_fidelity_a: Semeakoko Tablet 10 inch Tablet 1080P HD Tablet 64GB Storage, Quad-core 3GB RAM, 6000mAh Long-Lasting Battery, 2MP+8MP Dual Camera, WiFi Tablet Android10.0 Tablet 10 inch with Case Included This is the third tablet I've tried recently. On the plus side, it has some nice accessories that didn't come with the other two tablets. Those include a case, a stylus, and a screen protector. For the Fire and other Android tablets I tried, those all had to be bought separately. I did have some practical issues with this tablet though. The more serious one is that I have trouble keeping it charged up. Sometimes it seems to charge just fine. Other times I can't get it to turn on. A lesser but still irritating issue was with the stylus. When first setting up the tablet I had a lot of trouble entering the passcode for my wifi server. A dozen times I was unable to get the code loaded even though I was being careful to enter it correctly. It turned out that the stylus was, for some unknown reason, entering a symbol I had never seen before instead of an s. When I used my fingers, instead of the stylus, to enter the code, it worked perfectly and I was finally able to connect the tablet to the internet. I don't know if the stylus and the charging glitches are something I am doing wrong or some problem with this tablet, so I'm giving it a neutral three star rating. Check the other reviews. If I am the only one having these issues, then it's likely just me. If, on the other hand, others are reporting similar problems, you may want to hesitate about buying this product.
text_fidelity_b: Semeakoko Tablet 10 inch Tablet 1080P HD Tablet 64GB Storage, Quad-core 3GB RAM, 6000mAh Long-Lasting Battery, 2MP+8MP Dual Camera, WiFi Tablet Android10.0 Tablet 10 inch with Case Included

EPN Laptop Stand, Adjustable Laptop Riser with USB Cooling Fan, Ergonomic Computer Stand for Desk, Compatible with MacBook Pro Air, Dell, HP, Lenovo, More 9-16" Laptops, Aluminium Silver The EPN adjustable laptop stand is constructed of heavy-duty aluminum and feels sturdy. I tried it with both my 2017 15" Intel MB Pro and the redesigned 2020 16" MB Pro with a thicker bottom case.

I tend to lean my hands on the edge of my laptop, so I found the rise on the edge to be somewhat high when using it with my older computer, although I do appreciate having the extra fans for cooling on that model because Intel Mac Books Pro models tend to overheat.

This stand can handle the weight of both machines, with the latter coming in at over 4lbs, along with the weight of my hands leaning on it, and there was no indication of it wanting to sag or sink in any way. It will stay put at whatever angle or height you choose. At least it did for me.

I like having a slight angle when I type, and being able to raise my screen's camera to eye level so I am not looking down at it during Zoom meetings for that double chin effect. It's also convenient to have that little nook of space to tuck any cables and SSDs underneath, and out of the way.

There is about an inch to two inches of overhang on either side with larger computers, but it's not much, and both computers felt stable.

Overall, I would say it's a very good, and high-quality laptop stand. However, it is a bit smaller than I expected.

text_fidelity_a:
Cleaning Gel 160G, Dust Cleaning Mud for Car, Car Accessories, Keyboard Printers Cameras PC Tablet Laptop Airpods Case Cleaner EDIT: added pictures.

Not bad, about what I imagined having never used a gel glob like this before (but having wanted to for a long time!).

I have only used it on my keyboard. It is my main reason for acquiring it. I am always grossed out by how my keyboard looks. I sometimes use canned air (but ran out) and disinfectant wipes. I really just wanted to see if I could do better with a cleaning glob. I just wanted to know!

It did a great job with the surface of the keys. They look polished and shiny, and not at all greasy nor grimy. I would say it took more effort to get further down the sides, but I may have been too careful/light with my effort. I think next time I will really pressed into the keys and hopefully I can just work the stuff down the sides easier. Going forward, I would still use canned air to get anything out that is deeper down below the keys. And, still using a disinfectant wipe is a good idea these days. I think I will use this as maintenance rather than for going after a super gross keyboard. I like the scent- it smells fresh and clean. Doesn't linger, but while using it it is rather nice.

The look of it after using it to clean my keyboard really makes me want to hurl. I am not sure how often this can be reused, or if it would be better as a one time project use. I mean, it is meant to be used over and over, just not sure if I want to. Again, I think I like the idea of using it as a maintenance item if I plan to use it over and over. There is a little diagram on the container showing how to check if it needs replacing. It doesn't say much, but I surmise that if it goes from the bright color to a dark color, then it needs to be replaced.

Anyway, I think it is worth the try. It really does grab onto the nasty things and pulls it off/out. This wasn't too pricey, and I think stuff like this could be added on to a themed gift- like a car/truck lovers gift, an office supplies gift, and so on. Who knows.

There is some info on the container (a small clear plastic container with screw on lid, and labeling all around) that I will list here:

Directions say:
-- "Do not rub just press!" as well as, "Use with body hands" (lost in translation? maybe means both hands, or put your body into it?)

--Absorbs dirt and dust in cavities. Ideal for all devices and surfaces

--Keep away from direct sunlight and keep in a dry place. Keep away from children, don't eat it

--Ingredients:
Vegetable gum, Bactericide, Quaternium, fragrance, glycerin.

--Made in China
text_fidelity_b: Cleaning Gel 160G, Dust Cleaning Mud for Car, Car Accessories, Keyboard Printers Cameras PC Tablet Laptop Airpods Case Cleaner

text_fidelity_a:
CableMod C-Series Classic ModMesh Sleeved Cable Kit for Corsair Type 4 RM Black Label/RMi/RMX (White) I purchased these for the RM650x in my new build. to clean up the appearance of my case, as the default Corsair cables are serviceable but neither flexible nor visually appealing. Do I have a fancy case? It's a Fractal Define Mini C, so, sorta. Do I have a side window? No. Will anyone ever see the interior of this case aside from me and randos and I'm flexing on? Certainly not.

Why get cables like these? Call it an eccentricity. I don't like chaos hiding right out of sight. Sure, the Mini C would have the outward appearance of a stocky monolith of unalloyed order, but inside there would be a twisting madness of PVC and copper, heaving silently against the surface. There would be no evidence of it, sure, but I would know.

I would know.

So anyway, I purchased these to extend the relentless teleology of the IC into the broader world, and to this end I was successful. The cables are much more flexible than the default ones and the paracord is an interesting contrast against the typical circuit boards and enameled aluminum panels. They are a bit pricey for what you get, that's definitely the case - you might be better served by getting a different brand or shorter extensions rather than the full PSU set. I just happened to have the money for the CableMods.

Caveats: if you are using velcro ties inside the case, then you have to be careful with the ModFlex, as the hook-side can pull threads from it. I presume ModMesh, being nylon, would not have that issue. to get around it, I used rubber/silicon bands, since unlike zipties they can be removed and adjusted relatively easily.

Would I recommend them? If you have a side-window or transparent case, they are a definitely aesthetically on point. ModFlex or ModMesh, either should be suitable. If not, unless you too are eccentric, it probably isn't worth it. The improvement in airflow and the reduction in strain on the components are minimal so long as you are implementing reasonable cable management techniques. I'm still happy I purchased them though, since I'm pretty sure I'll be able to use them in the next two-three builds and they did make it a bit easier to get everything where I wanted it.
text_fidelity_b: CableMod C-Series Classic ModMesh Sleeved Cable Kit for Corsair Type 4 RM Black Label/RMi/RMX (White)

VIMVIP USB Microphone, Microphone for Computer USB Mic for PC Desktop Laptop Condenser Microphone to Recording Podcast Gaming Streaming YouTube A warning to first time users, you may experience the microphone picking up background noise. It's very sensitive. Be prepared to set-up an area for recording if you are wanting to get clean audio. The VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone came in a fairly plain box with a large hard foam protective insert. This microphone seems to be a great starting point for anyone interested in a higher quality microphone. I can whole heartedly recommend it.

The VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone is a USB interface microphone that is a large step-up in quality to those used to the basic microphones that come with many web cameras. It provides a higher sensitivity to sounds; enabling both a greater ability to pick up lower volume noises and the ability to comprehend higher volume ones.

The lower volumes it was able to obtain included whispering, including the mouth noises associated with ASMR videos, and keystrokes from a non-mechanical keyboard roughly 6 feet away [With it's recording volume turned down to 50%]. On the higher end of volume it is able to accommodate singing, yelling, and screaming; by not topping out what it able to accommodate this allowed for wide arrays of vocals and would assist with those wanting to record instruments. I did many different experiments to test the range at home on different days.

The VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone came with a short stand and pop filter that is attached to the stand by goose neck. The stand and metallic goose neck are both adjustable to assist with angling, but it is not vertically adjustable. The microphone, when pointing directly up, is about 26 cm / 10 in in height to the top of the microphone. It has a rubber ball footed desktop tripod for stability. The microphone can also detach from the included stand and be mounted to a standard size tripod or any other compatible stand, making the pop filter necessary depending on setup.

I had a great experience using VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone to audition for a voice acting role organized by fellow fans of an animated series. The VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone certainly made me sound much better than my webcam microphone is able to do. I have been using this for cooperative game-play online as well. This is a great value, especially at the price point.

Thank you for reading my review. I hope you have found it informative and helpful.
text_fidelity_b: VIMVIP USB Microphone, Microphone for Computer USB Mic for PC Desktop Laptop Condenser Microphone to Recording Podcast Gaming Streaming YouTube

text_fidelity_a:
ARCTIC Breeze Pro USB Desktop Fan with 4-Port USB Hub This review covers two different models of the Arctic fan:

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>Model with USB hub:
I have been using the original ARCTIC Breeze for a while and have been very pleased with its performance, and especially pleased with how quiet it runs. The Pro model builds on that and adds a few more useful features.

Unlike the original model which had a bendable stem with a USB plug on the end, the Pro has a base so the fan can be positioned away from the USB port on the PC. The attached power cord is a little over 5 feet long, making it possible to put the fan on my desk and plug it into the PC on the floor.

The base also has 4 USB input ports, so it works as a USB hub. It has a 5V power input jack if you want to turn this into an active hub. The power adapter to do so is NOT included.

Unlike the single-speed original version, this has a knob so you can vary the speed. It's not precise, but there is a somewhat noticeable difference between low and high. It's a continually variable speed - you can turn the dial to whatever speed you like.

Best of all, it's just as quiet, if not quieter, than the original model. That's the biggest plus for me by far, since the cheap USB fans make a racket. This just makes a low-pitched hum. The build quality is solid - the base is sturdy, and the bendable arm holds its position well.

One negative: the packaging. It's in a clam shell package that is a major, major pain to open!

While it's more expensive than the original, the added benefits of being able to position it on a desk and use it as a hub makes the upgrade worth considering. Highly recommend.

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>USA EDITION:
I've have (and use) a couple other Arctic USB fans and have been 100% satisfied with them. This new version (their "USA Edition") has a couple of improvements over past designs.

The base is a metal plate which increases the fan's stability when you're bending the stem to point the fan. The on/off/speed dial switch no longer has a lit LED ring around it. I never found the lit LED ring to be bothersome on the other Arctic fans, so having or not having it is not a big deal to me.

The base also does away with the USB hub connections that other models have. That's keeps the base more streamlined and allows it to have a lower profile. It also does away with the clam shell packaging, instead using a very easy to open box.

The build quality of this, like the other Arctic fans I have, is excellent. The stem is bendy by stays put where you want it; the operating sound is pretty hushed; the on/off/speed control works well. The overall design is attractive, with a red/white/blue color scheme and graphics.

It moves a surprising amount of air. No, it won't blow your hair back as a Vornado fan will, but this makes a noticeable difference in circulating air. The size makes it very easy to find a spot on your desk to position it.

While I can't speak to the long-term reliability of this as of yet, I expect it will last for some time. I have an Arctic fan similar to this that I've been using almost daily for the past 1+ years, and it still works as good as it did when new.

Looks good, works well, and easy to use. Highly recommend.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: ARCTIC Breeze Pro USB Desktop Fan with 4-Port USB Hub

Aoybevty USB C to USB C 3.1/3.2 Cable 6FT, 10Gbps Data Transfer 100W Fast Charging 4K@60Hz Video Monitor Cable for Thunderbolt 4/3 Laptop Tablet Cell Phone USB Type C Electronics Devices This usb type-c to type-c cable is costs a little more than other cables you may see because it is not just a charging cable.

When it comes to the Type-C port, consumers now need to have a phd in electronics just to understand what works with what. There are just so many standards crammed into this reversible port that you need to really read the fine print to know whether it will work for your uses. What's worse is that once you throw these cables into a drawer, good luck finding the right one.

Type-C cables that come with your phone or phone charger will generally only be good for charging your phone, but not great for transferring data. This Type-C cable will carry up to 100w of power, meaning it will charge your phone or tablet at the highest speed it can support. When transferring data, this cable will allow you to copy files at the highest USB 3.1 speeds.

But more than that, this cable supports video signals so that it will be usable to connect your laptop or phone to a portable type-c monitor (assuming your devices support it).

Personally, I got this cable to work with a pair of NReal Air video glasses so that I have a backup to the cable included in the box. These cables work but are a little bit stiff.

Kingston 64GB DataTraveler Elite G2 Black Metal Casing Fast 180MB/s R, 70MB/W USB 3.1 Flash Drive with LED light indicator (DTEG2/64GB) This is an unremarkable USB drive, with unexciting performance, for an unattractive price. (That's pretty much it for the substance of the review.)

I do my tests on a pretty fast computer with tons of memory, and an SSD system drive, while I'm doing nothing else on the computer, so no system resource constraints should affect the results. I test writes from SSD to USB, and reads in the other direction. I also use a set of 2GB test files, so that I get true results (small files can give misleading results).

I saw writes to the USB drive going between 4.5 and 8 MB/s, which is really pretty slow. I can get 16+ consistently on a little Lexar 32GB drive I have lying around. And a quick look in Amazon shows that I can find much faster USB3 drives for a bit less or a bit more, promising about 5x the write performance.

Finally, the form factor is terrible. This is a big fat ugly drive, you can get higher capacity and much better performance in slim little drives, including nano-drive size products.

Bottom line, it's ok, but I can't recommend it.
text_fidelity_b: Kingston 64GB DataTraveler Elite G2 Black Metal Casing Fast 180MB/s R, 70MB/W USB 3.1 Flash Drive with LED light indicator (DTEG2/64GB)

Baseus USB-C Docking Station, USB C Data Hub Adapter with PD Type C Charging Port, 5-in-1 USB C Dongle Adapter for MacBook/Pro/Air 2018,Chromebook,XPS,Galaxy S10/S9/S8/Note9 This is a review for the Baseus 5-in-1 USB C Hub. I have a few different hubs now because Apple decided I only needed USB-C ports on my laptop. Depending on what I’m doing and how many devices I need to plug in, I’ll either use a hub or adapters.

WiFi signal strength can be impacted by hubs or similar devices, there’s some interference with USB 3.0 and 2.4Ghz networks. It’s a known problem, there’s a lot about it online if you’ve also run into it. I’ve noticed this using other hubs, and I have about the same degree of interference with this one.

I don’t love the design of this hub. I wish the hub’s USB-C plug was straight, not an “L.” While I can still plug in other USB-C things next to the hub, the “L” shape of the plug dictates how the hub sits on my desk.

The hub is bigger than it needs to be. Maybe if the glassy front was repurposed, the USB 3.0 ports laid out in a square rather than a line, it wouldn’t take up as much room on my desk. The big display only has a tiny icon to show me when the hub is on … I just don’t like the wasted space.

text_fidelity_a:
Fixcracked for iPad mini & iPad mini 2 9.7 inch Touch Screen Replacement Parts Digitizer Glass Assembly+ Professional Tool Kit (black) The gist: the kit is about 85% complete, the glass is easy to install, and it all works well.

I'd almost give this kit 5 stars except for a few salient omissions: the lack of instructions, and a couple of parts which I think should have been included.

There are no instructions included in the kit, and the ones in this listing are garbage. Look to other sources for how to replace the digitizer.

Everything that is included is of adequate quality, and everything was useful. I needed to provide a heat gun and safety glasses (do wear safety glasses, prescription glasses would work just as well, or a face shield--i had little pieces of glass pinging me in the face as I removed the very cracked digitizer).

All told the replacement took me 3 hours to complete. I followed instructions on the iFixit site; there were a few discrepancies but fairly trivial ones, and it included many tips, cautions, and comments, in addition to the directions, that were more than adequate to make the repair fairly easy. As I mentioned, the glass was a mess of cracks, I covered the screen with a couple of layers of packaging tape to hold the majority of shards together as I worked. Once the glass was off everything went pretty smoothly.

The two things which I think should have been included are adhesive and gloves. The glass is taped down, and at least in my case, the tape is almost impossible to recover. The gloves would make keeping the screen and glass free of finger prints. Both would be pretty cheap.
text_fidelity_b: Fixcracked for iPad mini & iPad mini 2 9.7 inch Touch Screen Replacement Parts Digitizer Glass Assembly+ Professional Tool Kit (black)

LeadsaiL Rechargeable Wireless Computer Mouse, 2.4G Portable Slim Cordless Mouse Less Noise for Laptop Optical Mouse with 5 Adjustable DPI Levels USB Mouse for Laptop, Deskbtop, MacBook I'll be honest, I was expecting this to be another cheap off-brand mouse. I'm pleasantly surprised at how good it is- It looks pretty great, and rather than being covered in shiny fingerprint-magnet plastic like most cheap mice, a majority of the surface is textured (almost like a rubberized plastic). The USB receiver fits inside the body of the mouse for storage, which is great for travelling with it as I do. I've owned other mice that did that before too (an old Logitech), but unlike that old Logitech, this one uses a built-in rechargeable battery. To be honest, my Logitech mouse was great but after a couple of years the battery started making a bad connection inside (corroded contacts were keeping the battery from working), so I'd have to try to clean it off every few uses on the road to keep it working. With this product however, it seems less likely that will become a problem. Also, the ability to plug it in and charge it off the computer directly if it starts to die is a great plus!
My first impression was that the mouse was a little jumpier than I expected, but then I noticed the little button under the scroll wheel and discovered that it was for changing the DPI. Honestly, I'm not sure why they put it in such an easy to use spot, I feel like this isn't something that needs to change very often. Synsen Replacement Ear Pads Cushion Compatible for Bose QuietComfort QC2,QuietComfort 15 QC15,QuietComfort QC25,QuietComfort 35 QC35,Bose AE2,AE2i,AE2w,SoundTrue, SoundLink (Around-Ear) Headphones I purchased these replacement pads for my Bose QC-15 headphones as the old pads were torn and needed to be replaced. I selected this set of pads based on the positive reviews here on Amazon with the thought that they would be the same as the original pads. While they look the same, they are indeed slightly different.

First things first - these pads are fairly easy to install though they do require a little persistence to get them to snap into place. The earphones themselves have small tabs around the edges designed to snap the pads' bases into place and hold securely, and if the pads are not snapped down they simply will not stay securely. The inner foam and cloth shield that covers the electronics is easy to install but I had trouble with the double-sided tape that holds them in place - the adhesive did not want to release the cover strip and I had real difficulty peeling that strip away without ripping the actual cloth.

Once in place, the phones look exactly like they did when they were new, but I found three differences. First, the phones no longer fit into the case as easily as they once did. Instead of just turning the cups to lay flat and simply putting them in the case, now I have to mess with them slightly to fit into the case properly, though they can be made to fit. More noticeable, though, is that the pads are not as effective as the originals for passive noise canceling. A fan that I have in my office used to be canceled out almost completely with the combination of passive and active noise canceling but is now more audible than when the original pads were in place. I would not say the difference is enough to render the earphones' ability to cancel noise completely compromised, but they are definitely not the same. Finally, these replacement pads are just a little less supple and soft than the original pads. It is not all that noticeable until comparing the original and replacement pads side by side. You have to really be looking closely for the difference to notice it, but it's there.

The difference in noise canceling ability is most noticeable when working in an environment with reverb. I use my phones to monitor sound coming through a professional sound board because these have always done an excellent job of eliminating reverb and leaving just what comes through the sound board. With these new pads in place, I can now hear a lot of reverb, even when I press the phones tight over my ears and have ensured that they completely cover my ears so it's not a gapping issue. The material is different, plain and simple.

These are not bad replacement pads by any means. They are very good, they are comfortable and they do make these phones look brand new again. That said, they were not manufactured by Bose and there are some differences. When considering the cost difference between these and Bose parts, the trade-offs balance out favorably. If you have to have an exact match with the original pads, these are very close but not 100% identical. If you are satisfied with a [roughly] 90%-95% match, these pads work nicely for a lot less than original manufacturer pads.
text_fidelity_b: Synsen Replacement Ear Pads Cushion Compatible for Bose QuietComfort QC2,QuietComfort 15 QC15,QuietComfort QC25,QuietComfort 35 QC35,Bose AE2,AE2i,AE2w,SoundTrue, SoundLink (Around-Ear) Headphones

Garmin Forerunner 110 GPS-Enabled Unisex Sport Watch (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I did a lot of research before making this purchase. Each day you run the watch has to reset position (unless you just wear it throughout the day). Do not hit the GPS button until you are outside and clear of your home/building. A couple of times I tried to get a jump start on the watch and hit the button while getting ready inside. My run was off by nearly 200 feet. It recharges very quickly so if you run in the morning and at night, you will easily have a full charge prior to your second run...typically takes 3 hours or so for a full charge from completely dead.
Definitely recommend the watch, especially for beginner and intermediate runners.

Logitech Harmony 650 Infrared All in One Remote Control, Universal Remote Logitech, Programmable Remote (Silver) I recently purchased this to replace a lost remote for a piece of high end integrated amp. As with most things in the audiophile world, a replacement for this simple 6 button remote was way overpriced ($105) for what it is. So I was pleased to find that my amplifier was supported by the Logitech 650.

My biggest gripe is nearly a dealbreaker. After setting it up I went to use it on my integrated amplifier to raise the volume a little bit. The problem was that I couldn't just give the volume button a quick tap to turn up the volume a little bit. A quick tap of the volume raised the volume a significant amount whereas the original amp controller allowed me to make volume changes in small increments. After some searching I found that I just had to adjust the IR repeat length in the controller setup.

Problem solved, right? Wrong.

First issue was the manual being outdated. The frustration started when I tried following the steps in the manual. The first step was "Click Troubleshoot at the top of the Harmony Remote Software window". The problem was that there was no Troubleshoot button anymore. They had updated the software but didn't update the manual. Eventually I found the new location in the software where you can lower the repeats. The default was set to 1 so I lowered it to 0 (the lowest setting on the 0-4 scale). I saved my changes and after waiting for the remote to update I tried it again and it still was making large volume changes. With the remote already set to the lowest setting the only way I can make small adjustments to volume is to press the volume button and cover the IR emitter on the remote extremely fast so the volume change signal only gets sent out for a quick burst. I'm talking ninja fast. This is extremely annoying and tricky to get the hang of.

PROS
-Price
-Device Compatibility

CONS
-Can't make small volume changes
-Outdated Manual (they updated the software but didn't update the PDF manual with new instructions for the new software). This causes some serious frustration when you are instructed in Step 1 to press a Troubleshooting button that no longer exists.

Final thoughts... I bought this to mainly do one thing. Change volume and input selection on my integrated amp. The inability to change the volume in small increments is a constant annoyance. It should be something that can be fixed with a software or firmware update.

Logitech, please fix this on the software/firmware side.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Harmony 650 Infrared All in One Remote Control, Universal Remote Logitech, Programmable Remote (Silver)

ADJUSTABLE! - THIS was a BIG deal to me because I wasn't sure EXACTLY how high I wanted it (I have an adjustable computer chair re height). HAS VENTILATION HOLES - for those wanting to put their desktop on it, this could be important that it has the holes in it.

BOTTOMLINE: I got it when it was two dollars off, so a total of about $15, but would have gladly paid more because it's perfect for what I wanted.

Throughout the day I repeated the test and the watch was constantly reading that my blood pressure was high, even after I had taken my medication and I know the readings should have changed.  I will have to get with my doctor/nurse and have them do a manual test and see if the watch is showing the same results.  If the watch bp monitor is not accurate, I have not been able to find any way to recalibrate the watch to input the correct bp reading.  That is the only problem I have with this watch.  I like all the features the watch has along with the phone app too.  It doesn't take long to learn all the functions of the watch as well as the app.  If you have high blood pressure, I wouldn't rely on just the watch to monitor your blood pressure because I don't believe it is accurate enough. text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Harmony Smart Control with Smartphone App and Simple All in One Remote - Black Build and Setup:
This is a very solid remote. Well constructed. It takes a disk watch type battery that is activated when you remove the tab. The lines are clean and elegant, and it feels well constructed.

Set up was very simple. I simply logged into myharmony.com and choose the Add a remote option.

The difference between this remote and other Harmony remotes is that this has a hub and blaster units that connects through your wireless network to allow you to connect and control your units with your smartphone.

You have to connect the hub and blaster unit around the units you want to control. It has to be connected to your home wireless network, which was easy. You can either do it through myharmony.com or by pressing the setup button on the hub and your router (if it supports it) it was that easy.

This particular unit controls my TV, Dish DVR, and VCR/DVD combo. Setting it up for the units was quite easy.

Using the Remote:
One selling point this has over the Ultimate is that the number buttons are solid state buttons, unlike the touch screen buttons on the Ultimate. As much as I like the touch screen technology, having buttons you can press by touch is a plus for.

There are also traditional DVR buttons, fast forward, as well as red, blue yellow, and green buttons. Since this remote did not have a 30 second advance button, and I rely on that, I programmed a short press of the green and yellow buttons to act as the skip forward. I programmed long pressing those buttons to do the default actions of those buttons. I appreciated that you could customize in that way.

Phone App:
The phone app for the android is a bit lacking as it is not quite as sophisticated as the remote itself, but can do most of the actions of the remote as long as you are connected to the same wireless network as your hub is.

Troubleshooting:
The remote is easy to use and troubleshoot, Simply rebooting or re-syncing the remote can resolve most problems I've found. It also prompts you for assistance the first time you add an action or new device.

Overall this is a great remote. This will demand, though, some knowledge on your part as it is a very sophisticated remote. Many problems that occur can easily be resolved by some knowledge of networks, remotes, or Harmony devices in general. If you have experience with this you will enjoy the functions and capacity of this remote.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Harmony Smart Control with Smartphone App and Simple All in One Remote - Black

text_fidelity_a:
Dell Inspiron Gaming PC Desktop AMD Ryzen 7 2700 Processor, 16GB DRAM, 1TB HDD, AMD Radeon RX 580 4GB GDDR5 Graphics Card, Windows 10 64-bit, Blue LED, Model Number: i5676-A696Blu I benchmarked using 3DMark, Time spy. From the results you can see it falls about where you would expect for its hardware and pricepoint. You are going to do better than an entry level gaming laptop, but you aren't going to be blowing anyone out of the water. But... this comp isn't really made for high performance.

It did handle both Minecraft and Ark. If you have kids you may have run into issues with Minecraft being RAM greedy, which is why you want at least 8GB and this has 16GB. So it will handle it with most mods pretty well.

Ark is terrible on computers. Even high end gaming rigs can struggle with it. It is one of the reasons I used it for testing. It is so poorly optimized that it will crash your PC and chuckle at your demise. This computer handled it well on medium settings, which isn't too bad. I wouldn't run epic settings on anything short of a NASA computer, and even still I'd be worried it would crash the space station or accidentally launch missiles.

Bottomline; this computer will make most games playable, they will not be "epic". It's a decent entry level gaming computer. I am not going to tell you to build your own if you want to save money and get a better set up for the same amount. Honestly, if you were of the mindset to do that you would not be considering $700 Dell computers. I have built my own computer, I have also wanted to throw it on the lawn and light it on fire, because when something goes wrong I have no one to blame but myself, and no one to fix it either. So... ignore the "build it yourself" shamers. You do you. If you want to buy an entry level gaming computer go for it. I would strongly recommend saving up the additional $250 to get the upgraded version of this computer though. For not much more, you get a whole heck of a lot more computer. Better processor, better graphic card, way better storage, and an SSD to run your operating system.

I knocked a star for the price and because the driver update software they have on there is a joke. I had to go manually update drivers myself. If that's not your deal I recommend adding a 3rd party driver updater, do not rely on Dells. If you are feeling brave you can buy a more powerful gaming computer for $700, you will just have to do a bit more research that they are a legitimate company.
text_fidelity_b: Dell Inspiron Gaming PC Desktop AMD Ryzen 7 2700 Processor, 16GB DRAM, 1TB HDD, AMD Radeon RX 580 4GB GDDR5 Graphics Card, Windows 10 64-bit, Blue LED, Model Number: i5676-A696Blu

text_fidelity_a: Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo, Black Colorful Retro 2.4GHz Typewriter with Cute Round Keycaps, DPI Adjustable Optical Compatible PC Laptop First let me say that I grew up typing on actual typewriters and I find myself getting really nostalgic about those days the older I get.  Not that I mind sleek, modern keyboards.  I do a great deal of writing, so I have adapted to the various styles as they've come out.  This particular keyboard is nice and pleasant to work on, but I wouldn't say it's a true typewriter style experience.  The keys are too flat and too round for that.  If you are like me and you do a lot of typing and can adapt yourself quickly between different keyboards you will probably enjoy this one.  I do find myself making a lot of typos that I normally wouldn't when I'm working on it though.  The mouse is honestly just annoying.  There is no actual switch to turn it off, just a button right on top that seems to 'wake' it when it goes dormant, so if you're prone to bumping it around or accidentally dropping things on it or if you plan on using it in multiple places for any reason whatsoever you will find yourself getting frustrated with just how easy it is to turn it back on.  The scroll wheel is fantastic, but the one on my previous mouse no longer works at all, so that might be the reason why I like it so much.  The accuracy of its tracking leaves a lot to be desired and it's quite loud when you click it, but I do tend to prefer to keep my environment quiet.  All in all I would not purchase this again both because the keyboard design is just 'off' in enough nit-picky ways to make it frustrating (so many typos) and because the mouse tracking and lack of a true 'off' switch makes it frustrating to actually use it.  Both the keyboard and the mouse are really pretty to look at and well built for what they are, but I wouldn't call them truly functional even though they do work.  If you're just doing minor browsing and not a lot of typing they would be fine for that, but if you're someone that does a lot of writing or anything that requires precision tracking of the mouse like playing games or working in paint programs you should probably skip this set.
text_fidelity_b: Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo, Black Colorful Retro 2.4GHz Typewriter with Cute Round Keycaps, DPI Adjustable Optical Compatible PC Laptop

Renegade Concepts: Lap PRO - Stand/Caddy Universal Beanbag Lap Stand Tablet Accessory for iPad 1, iPad 2, iPad 3, iPad 4, Acer, Nexus & All Android Tablets, E-Readers, Books & Google Devices (Blue) The LAP PRO universal tablet stand doesn't work very well with my Kindle Fire HD 8.9" Wi-Fi tablet. The stand consists of a very firm, 18-inch wide, cylindrical pillow with a soft handle that doubles as a sort of tray for the tablet. Because there is no frame to hold the tablet securely, the tablet must be set carefully into the handle-tray, and then the tablet simply leans against the pillow for support. However, the tablet is very easily dislodged from the tray, even when the stand is sitting on a flat tabletop.

Out of the box, the LAP PRO holds the 8.9" Kindle Fire HD tablet at a near-vertical angle that is uncomfortable for viewing or for using a stylus on the touch screen. There is a sheet packed with the pillow that says: "Your LAP PRO has come slightly over filled intentionally, which may interfere with some functions. This will change in time. This is to ensure it will perform properly and last longer after it breaks in. The fabric will stretch and the beans settle from use." However, this is not really a beanbag stand. The pillow is filled with something that feels like medium-fine sand (not beans). Also, the pillow is too firm to accommodate its shape to an uneven surface the way a beanbag does.

To adjust the tablet viewing angle, you must reshape the pillow--it isn't enough to simply roll the pillow forward or backwards. Because the pillow is so firm, you must exert some effort in reshaping. It is easier to adjust the pillow shape and the viewing angle if you unzip the zipper that runs alongside the handle-tray, but then the pillow kind of flops around. (The zipper is there to open and close a compartment that is probably intended to hold your tablet, because the LAP PRO is also supposed to be a "caddy".)

If I needed a travel pillow (another of the LAP PRO's advertised uses) or a tablet caddy, I might end up liking the LAP PRO. However, because the stand is too large for convenient tabletop use, is hard to adjust, doesn't hold the tablet securely, and needs break-in time, I rate it at 2 stars ("I don't like it" on the official Amazon scale).

EDITED 11/18/12: After hearing from the seller, Renegade Concepts, I believe that I may have received an overfilled LAP PRO. (Renegade Concepts offered to replace my unit.) If my LAP PRO had been less firm out of the box, I would have rated it at 3 stars ("It's OK").
text_fidelity_b: Renegade Concepts: Lap PRO - Stand/Caddy Universal Beanbag Lap Stand Tablet Accessory for iPad 1, iPad 2, iPad 3, iPad 4, Acer, Nexus & All Android Tablets, E-Readers, Books & Google Devices (Blue)

text_fidelity_a:
TiVo Roamio 500 GB DVR (Old Version) - Digital Video Recorder and Streaming Media Player Update. April 12, 2014. 4 months after purchase.

I have unplugged the TIVO, will pay the monthly fees for the next 8 months. At least I'll save the $ 3 month cable card fees.

I got another tuner. The tuner works. I have 2 TIVOs and the new tuner works in the old TIVO, but not the new Roamio. It is a Roamio problem.
I now only get 4 standard def stations with the Roamio.

TIVO offered to replace the Roamio for a flat $ 49, plus shipping. I figure the total cost will be $ 75. I'm sure I will get a refurbished TIVO.
Decided it wasn't worth spending $ 75 to get a refurbished TIVO, which may or may not work. Since my ROKU 3 gives me Time Warner Demand channels, it is much less compelling to have a TIVO.

I'll keep the TIVO Premiere connected as it has a lifetime and is trouble free, The Time Warner demand capability of the ROKU 3 is a major threat to TIVO's existence.

I did purchase the TIVO on Amazon with the AMEX credit card which doubles the warranty. I called AMEX. Was told it would not cover the cost of the replacement ($ 49). Only would cover the labor cost, since parts were still under the TIVO warranty (90 days labor, 1 year parts). Since labor isn't separately charged, I'm not covered. Think that stinks.

Update. 105 days later.

Well warranty is up by 15 days. TIVO doesn't recognize tuning adapter. My old premiere works perfectly.
Time Warner spent 2 hours at my home today, swapped out cable cards and tried 3 different tuning adapters. It's a TIVO issue.
I bypassed tuning adapter for a direct hookup. Gives me half the channels. When my one year committment is up, I'll scrap it.

Only saving grace. When I called to cancel my 13 month old Premier XL, they offered me a lifetime for $ 199. I took it.
Do not recommend it Roamio. I was one of the original TIVO users. A 45 hour standard definition TIVO. Very disappointed.

Original review.

Integrated Wi Fi. It's about time. This is my 4th TIVO. Currently paying for 2 monthly subscriptions. Have been satisfied with all my TIVOs. Getting rid of the $ 90 Wi Fi accessory is a big plus. Our other TIVO is a 2 tuner Premiere XL that holds 300 hours of HD. We've never had it over 25% , so 75 hours is enough for us. Our other TIVO has been moved to the bedroom. We really needed at least a 4 tuner set. Two tuners may seem enough, but the stations are now playing it cute by ending programs at 9:01 instead of 9. This causes a conflict and forces you to cancel a show, or not watch a live station at the same time. It effectively reduces the two tuner to a one tuner. Before your TIVO arrives, go to your cable source (if you use cable), and get the appropriate cable card for a 4 tuner set, and tuning adapter. TW charges me $ 2.80 each for the cards. One for each TV. You need to call your cable company to activate and pair your cable card. TW has a great system, and it took only minutes to do. You also need to have an HDMI cable on hand, and a USB to HDMI cable. The kind that connects from your wired printer to your computer.

I also pay monthly, not lifetime. On my original TIVO, an old 45 hour SD job, I took a $ 199 lifetime plan after 2 months. Three weeks later, a nearby lightning strike wiped out the modem on my TIVO, and my computer. Yes, I did have surge protectors, as well as a $ 300 whole house surge protector sold and installed by my electric company. End of my TIVO, end of my $ 199 lifetime plan. TIVO offered no sympathy. So TIVO yes. Lifetime plan NO.

You cannot stream to your mobile devices with the 4 tuner TIVO, without adding accessories.

Added. You also need a short coaxial cable. My prior TIVO packages included every possible cable you may need. No longer. The power supply, remote, remote batteries, and the TIVO were all that were included. An added explanation on the usb needed. The standard side of the USB connection connects to the TIVO. The printer type side connects to the tuning adapter. I went to my junk box, and pulled an old printer cable out. It's not the older type with the large ends. It is a very small odd sided type that plugs in. The cable company should be providing these. Ask them for one.
text_fidelity_b: TiVo Roamio 500 GB DVR (Old Version) - Digital Video Recorder and Streaming Media Player

text_fidelity_a: Yamaha RX-V679BL 7.2-Channel MusicCast AV Receiver with Bluetooth, Works with Alexa I purchased this AV receiver, Yamaha RX-V679BL 7.2-Channel MusicCast AV Receiver with Bluetooth, after my Onkyo failed, with no sound.  I read a lot of reviews and this unit seemed to be a good choice, just below another Yamaha newer model, the RX-V681.  I received it in about 3 days and placed it on a chair in front of my entertainment center to set it up and prove out the system before trying to place it where it was hard to get at in the entertainment cabinet opening above the TV.  After hooking up all the speakers, the Subwoofer, HDMI cables for the program sources and the HDMI output to the Led TV, I powered it on and it came up and the sound was there for the two front speakers and the center channel.  Sound volume was a pleasant surprise, as the Onkyo I had had was always lacking volume and delivery of the sound.  At this point, I had soured on Onkyo, but only after reading all the re-occurring sound issues from many previous models and that seem to continue on today.  I can't recommend the Onkyo, oversized receiver I had at this time or others as they discontinued the model I owned after I had bought it and it kind of just disappeared from existence.  This Yamaha runs much cooler and it just worked from the start.  I have downloaded my Owners manual from the Yamaha web support site and will study it in time.  It pleases me at this time and I will surely come back to this review when and if I need to, to update information and any concerns. I give it a 4 star review rating at this time and feel it is a good buy.
text_fidelity_b: Yamaha RX-V679BL 7.2-Channel MusicCast AV Receiver with Bluetooth, Works with Alexa

Cable Zip Ties 4 Inch, 1000Pcs Industrial Nylon Zip Ties | Durable Self Locking Wire Tie Wraps with 20 lbs Tensile Strength, Heat Resistant for Home Office Garage Multiple Use - White You know you are an adult when you get excited to add a big bag of zip ties to your home tool box. I have an assortment of zip ties in various sizes for various tasks. If you didn't know, it is better to go a little larger than what you think you need as the length indicated is entire length and not just working length. I just so happened to have had a need for the smaller size (6" or less) zip ties to secure some corners on a multi tier wire crate. I ratcheted them tight and trimmed off the excess. In all, I used about two dozen immediately. With a pack of 500 I should be set for awhile. Always better to have too many of these than not enough. I'll be using them for sure to secure snow netting. Not on the posts (need 10-12" ties for that), but to hold together the overlap going from one roll or piece to the next. Since a section of netting always gets blown apart at some point during the winter, I just head out with a handful of zip ties and put it back together again. So yeh, 500 seems like a lot, but when you have them you need a bunch of them.

The 6 inch size is also great for wire management in general, and just about any small sized securing needs.

No complaints. Happy to have them!
text_fidelity_b: Cable Zip Ties 4 Inch, 1000Pcs Industrial Nylon Zip Ties | Durable Self Locking Wire Tie Wraps with 20 lbs Tensile Strength, Heat Resistant for Home Office Garage Multiple Use - White
