text_fidelity_a:
USB DAC Audio Converter Headphone Amplifier Type-C Port Digital to Analog Signal Audio Converter, 3.5MM Stereo Audio Optical Headphone Jack Output, Type-C Input Not to shabby of a gadget. It's just a wee little thing- fits in the palm of my hand- a little smaller than a deck of cards. Is powered through whatever device you are using. Does not need to be separately powered or charged.

What's in the (generic) box:
--Amplifier unit (roughly measured at 3.5" x 2.5" x .75")
--Type C to Type C Cable
--Type C to USB Cable
--3.5mm to 2rca Cable
--User Manual (a piece of paper with info)

I also received some other cable assembly in the box that I do not know what it is for. Appears to be used in Optical port. Bonus in terms of what is listed in product description, I guess.

What is on the Amplifier unit:
--One end of unit has: Headphone input, On/Off Switch for Bass, Volume knob
--Other end of unit has USB C port (in), Optical port (out), Gain (H/L) Switch, Line Out port.

Connection Diagram shows use between SPEAKERS OR HEADPHONES, and Mobile phone, Laptop, computer, or PS4. States that it does not work with tv. I haven't tried it yet, but I may attempt a work around- I'll let you know if I am successful.

In mean time, I have tried it between my smartphone (Pixel4XL) using AmazonMusic and two different types of speakers.

The first set of speakers is a nice plug in variety. They are circa 2004 CambridgeSoundWorks- where one cord is plugged into wall receptacle , and the other plug goes into a headphone port. They sound nice with use with my phone, so I didn't expect much difference when adding this amplifier. True enough, they have similar quality. My speakers without the amplifier are loud and I can hear some range. The addition of the amplifier allowed me to manipulate the bass, which can be nice depending on what I am listening to. I switched between High and Low on the gain switch. High boosts the overall sound, and low brings out a more mellow tone. Either are good.

Next, I tried it with a pair of novelty speakers circa 2002. Little SONYspeakers that are really just a headphone style output. So for purpose of review, using these is to mimic a set of basic headphones. They just happen to be in the shape of a speaker sitting on a desk rather than on the head. Cute little things, and when plugged into anything they really produce no further sound advantage over a basic set of headphones other than they aren't on the head. Thought these would be perfect to see how much this amplifier can help a bare bones basic sup par listening item. The sound went from a very low, just make out the music sound to truly being amplified. I could boost the volume and the sound opened up- not just got louder. So, while I will likely never use it with these, I thought hearing the difference on a terrible set of "speakers" (again, really just non head headphones) was absolutely worth mentioning. Tells me that this product IS working as intended.

Now, my Pixel4XL has fair sound already- not nuance, but not sounding like a tin can either. Using this with my nicer plug in speakers is great. Using my phone, with my nicer speakers AND this amplifier is a little nicer, but not hugely so. Perhaps in a larger room, or in other conditions where I may need a more dynamic sound to carry. This isn't a knock on the product, I think it is a nod toward the quality of my old speakers. I definitely can hear the improvement with ability to boost bass. High to high sounds similar. My speakers can't display a low end gain. So good for this product to offer that.

I do happen to have a speaker hooked up to my TV, and I am going to try to make that work if it doesn't complicate my wire management.

As for cord length.. if you are using it with your headphones, this is fine. You would otherwise be plugging it into the headphone port on your device, so really, with addition of the amplifier and the other cord to connect to device, you gain several extra inches of length. Beyond that, your mileage may vary in terms of what will work for you.

So far so good.

PS, I had low expectations of this unit, so I am impressed with my experience so far. As I continue to try it out with various devices in various environments, if I learn anything new-- good, bad, helpful, enlightening, I will surely be back to share.

I think it is worth trying out. I can't comment on price as I am not sure what these are really worth, and if there are true differences among the options out there. So my rating is based purely on effectiveness of product and accuracy of product description. If I had one wish on the options provided on this product, that would be to allow some additional range in the High/Low gain switch. I'd give this 4.5 stars, but since it is whole numbers only- 5 it is (unless I need to change it over time through learning something new about it).
text_fidelity_b: USB DAC Audio Converter Headphone Amplifier Type-C Port Digital to Analog Signal Audio Converter, 3.5MM Stereo Audio Optical Headphone Jack Output, Type-C Input

myCharge PowerGear Sound Protective Portable Charging Case for Wireless Earbuds Headphones | Custom Tray Compatible with Powerbeats & Removable for Other Brands | 1400 mAh / 1A Output The MyCharge is a handy if not tiny clamshell charging case for PowerBeat headphones, though it will work for others as well.

Pros:
The case itself has an hard outer shell that feels durable and thick. I have no fears the earbuds will be well protected inside. It opens and closes easily and tightly. As much as a case can be, it’s aesthetically pleasing—a dark, slick black with a black ribbon with red stitching running down the middle (the red stitching matches the red inside). The ribbon/band does more than add a bit of style and color; it also gives it a bit more texture so it grips the surface it’s atop better.

The plastic tray inside is designed for the PoweBeats line, so the earbuds nestle snugly (but with no need to wrestle or force them in) into an indentation so they lie flat and with a mid-section to insert the connecting wires/controls into. It’s a good fit, well-designed, and I don’t feel like I’m overstressing the wires, though I wouldn’t want to leave them in that position for a long amount of time (though I tend to worry about that sort of thin more than others)

It comes with a cable. You can use any one, but you’ll want it to be very short

The port to charge the case (the battery inside the case for sticklers) is easily accessible.

An LED on the front lets you know if the case battery is getting low

Cons
I wish the port cover felt a little more durable

Mixed or Up in the Air
I haven’t had it long enough yet to check how many charges, but I’ve gotten a few without a noticeable impact on the case battery. I don’t know if their promise of a dozen-plus will bear out, but I don’t think it’ll be far off if not.

The case isn’t really tiny (You can see the dimensions above). If you’re looking for something to slip into a pocket, then this will be a con, though it will easily fit a coat pocket. It will fit cargo pockets but you’ll definitely know it’s there. On the other hand, it doesn’t take up a lot of space, it’s quite protective, and if you’re worried about losing your expensive but very small and easy to lose earbuds, putting them in a noticeable, protective case that will also charge them back up is far from the worst idea. Personally, I’m OK with the size.

As noted, the case is designed for PowerBeats, so your mileage will vary on how well it fits some other type. My other earbuds all fits in the case without an issue, just not as snugly or neatly. That isn’t a real priority for me even ignoring the fact that I have PowerBeats.

Overall, a good value for what it does I’d say.

text_fidelity_a:
Santana Samba by Carlos Santana, High Power Portable Bluetooth Speaker, 20W Outdoor Speaker, IP67 Dustproof & Waterproof Stereo Speakers, 20H Playtime, Powerful Extra Loud Volume with Rich Bass Our family is a bunch of speaker and ear phone fanatics. Everyone has different likes and I tend to like a well balanced music. Muffled really bugs me.

I wanted to have a nice balanced speaker that no one will take so I decided to get this one for ME. It has a nice solid housing and I figured it was worth getting since my favorite speaker seems to get misplaced a lot. Let's take a look.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This is a very solid speaker. It is heavy duty and it has metal housing. The sides are not as fragile as others I have used which sound this good. It comes in a beautiful gift box which has cushioning and the typical Santana design to it. The speaker itself is pretty heavy so it is not something you toss in your backpack and run off with. It needs a bit more care than that.

CHARGING
This has a USB charger that will take about 4 hours to charge it up with. There is also a connection where you can get a FAST charger from the company, but you have to contact them for it. The charging cable comes with it just need a USB outlet. The directions warn to only use the original cable that comes with this to charge or there might be damage to the speaker. The voltage must be 5V with current rated at 115A.

CAN THIS RUN WHILE CHARGING?
I do not see in the instructions warnings against this, and it does work while plugged in.

PLAY TIME
This speaker runs out of juice pretty quickly. If you want it to last the entire time of 10 hours, I highly suggest you not put the volume up past 30%. Any higher and the battery time runs down pretty quickly. At 60% you are at the edge of running this down pretty quickly- as in 4 or 5 hours play time only.

PAIRING
I have had no issues pairing this with tablets or phones using Android. Just like when you turn the power on, it says PAIRING in a very loud voice so you will know when it is in pairing mode.

VOLUME
The volume button on this is tricky. If you are not thinking and just quickly press the volume once, instead of it getting slightly louder, you will skip a track. You have to press the volume down and not let up if you want the sound to go up or down depending on the button you press meaning +/-.

CARD SLOT
This speaker can also work off of a TF card (also known as a microSD card). You just have to change from bluetooth mode to card mode using the MODE button.

IS THERE AUX CAPABILITY?
I have an old MP3 player that has higher quality recordings than anything new I have. That only uses AUX and it works great with this.

PAUSE / PLAY
You can pause or play music with this using the MFB button

HOW DOES THIS PERFORM?
Let me tell you, this thing ROCKS. I mean it. This speaker is fabulous. Not only does it work great out of the box (after being fully charged) but it sounds better and better as you break it in. It fills the house with music that is great quality and does not have interference or any lag issues either.

WHAT ABOUT BASS, MIDS AND HIGHS?
I have to say that this speaker is one of the few that I have used which does a beautiful job of intense bass, balanced clear highs but the mids are not muffled at all. It is impressive and what I thought a speaker always should be.

CAN YOU USE TWO TOGETHER?
This allows you to add one other speaker to the system so you can have them in two places. I do not have another Europa speaker at the moment I can test that with.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Although this blows any other wireless speaker I have had out of the water, it does blow through power rather quickly unless the volume is pretty low. It is not only amazing out of the box (After charging) but it gets better with more use. This baby ROCKS.

MY RATING
Finding a speaker which does not overwhelm you with out of whack bass, piercing highs, or muffled middles is not always easy. This speaker seems to divide it all out very well. It is one of the nicest speakers I have used (wireless) to date. FIVE STARS!

Not only do I love this, but would definitely consider a second one along with the fast charger in the future to round out the whole system.

ANOTHER THING
This product has a notification on it that some of the proceeds from this product will go to help underprivileged children through the MILAGRO foundation (miracle) that Carlos Santana and his family started in 1998.
text_fidelity_b: Santana Samba by Carlos Santana, High Power Portable Bluetooth Speaker, 20W Outdoor Speaker, IP67 Dustproof & Waterproof Stereo Speakers, 20H Playtime, Powerful Extra Loud Volume with Rich Bass

text_fidelity_a:
3M Quiet Space Headphones, Bluetooth Headphones, Wireless Headphones, 1 Pair Most of the headphones with which I have worked have been active noise canceling (ANC) phones so I know a lot about those, but I also have other headphones too that I like. I was unaware that 3M even had headphones, and I was also unsure what their "Quiet Space" was all about. It's an interesting solution that works fairly well. Overall, these are good phones, though there's one area that could use some slight improvement and that's the sound profile.

These are over-the-ear phones and they are actually quite comfortable. I like how they feel on my head - they fit snugly and I can tilt my head without losing these phones, but they don't clamp down super tight either.

Build-wise, these are more substantial than the price suggests. I like the size adjustment in particular which is designed to last and should not fatigue with use.

I powered these on and they quickly paired and connected to my laptop. The range is good and I was able to walk a fair distance away without losing the connection or having the sound get crackly or having it skip. With no feed coming to them they eventually powered themselves off, saving battery but potentially frustrating the wearer if this is unexpected.

Just putting these on I was surprised by the amount of noise isolation. Without even turning these on they drastically reduced the ambient noise in the room, even effectively blocking out the sound of a running fan. I have had very few headphones that have as effective sound isolation as these, and that's a huge plus right out of the gate. The Quiet Space function adds to this, but not like ANC phones - it injects white noise into the cans so all you hear is a gentle but constant hiss that overrides most other noises. It's not deathly quiet with these on, but you won't hear most other sounds in the area when they're producing white noise. This is a very different approach to sound cancellation and it works.

The sound profile is the one area where these phones could use a little improvement, though these are not terrible and are better than some big-name phones I have used. The bass is not overdriven but it is not muted either, and this is refreshing since most manufacturers overdrive the bass. The highs are clear, though not shrill. The midrange, however, is flat to the point that music can sound slightly hollow. It's an easy fix with an equalizer and is better than one particular big-name manufacturer's similar flaw.

I like these phones and will be working with them more. They take a different approach to dealing with ambient noise and surrounding distractions than what ANC phones use, and they seem to work well. They're well made, comfortable and reasonably priced.
text_fidelity_b: 3M Quiet Space Headphones, Bluetooth Headphones, Wireless Headphones, 1 Pair

Anker 2.4G Wireless Vertical Ergonomic Optical Mouse, 800 / 1200 /1600 DPI, 5 Buttons for Laptop, Desktop, PC, Macbook - Black Fortunately I bought this at a much cheaper price at $16 instead of the current price as of this writing at $27. There are lots of comparable wireless vertical ergonomic mice less than $27 that also include recharging and cool LED lights. Although it's a decent ergonomic vertical mouse, there are some legitimate gripes with this mouse after months of use so now I'm looking to try a different brand of vertical mouse.

The 2.4Ghz range is pretty bad. I found this out later down the road when I had to switch the USB dongle to a port on the back of my computer. At first I thought my batteries were low (or some dirt interfering with optical sensor) because my mouse cursor would stagger on and off as a moved cursor across screen. That was really frustrating not only for browsing but games. When I put the dongle closer to the front of computer it worked much better.

Now onto the batteries. This may be good or bad depending on preference but it uses AAA batteries. Although replacing batteries seems like an inconvenience, if you have a mouse with a built-in rechargeable lithium ion battery and the batteries go bad or defective then you would have to trash the whole mouse instead of just replacing the batteries.

There is a separate top button on the mouse for DPI toggle (800/1200/1600) but I can't tell what mode it is in unless I move the mouse across the screen every time I toggle it so it is kind of inconvenient. Would be nice so you can visually see the dpi on the mouse or on screen.

Overall, the mouse feel good upon touching it. The texture on the mouse is not glossy plastic but has a slight comfy texture on it. My personal gripe with the ergonomics is it feels a bit narrow and the hand does not feel relaxed. I think the culprit is the thumb rest position feels like it is a bit upwards causes your thumb to squeeze inward instead of relaxing. So I try not to point or put my thumb in the default thumb rest but more below the thumb rest or even slight bend my thumb so it's not straight and stiff.

Garmin nüvi 255 3.5-Inch Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I bought a new Nuvi 255 for my wife about two years ago. I liked it so much I bought another new one for myself last year. They are great units operationally, but both have exhibited failures. Early this summer, about 18 months of age for the 1st unit and 12 months for the second, they each failed to respond to their respective touchscreens within about a week of each other. I tried the reset button and initiating the touchscreen calibration procedure, but the problem prevailed.
I then connected the first unit to my PC through the USB port and the touchscreen began working afterward. The same cure worked on the second unit. Software glitch I thought.
Well, the older one now exhibits the same failure mode again, and nothing I do helps, including installing the latest firmware update from the Garmin site. I'm worried the other will permanently fail too.
As much as I like the operation of these units, I would not recommend any of the Garmin 2xx family for reliability reasons. I see from internet searches that the problem is not an isolated one. None of the posted "solutions" worked for me. I assume I am not alone. By the way, the frozen unit eventually bypasses the "legal" screen (times out I suppose) and goes into the map navigation mode, although it is still unresponsive to the touch screen.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin nüvi 255 3.5-Inch Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

* The back is clear, which allows you to showcase the Surface Pro 7's sleek encasement
* It has a fold-able cover that can be manipulated into a stand for the Surface when using it like a tablet
* The case's sides are made of a thick rubber that would provide some protection for the corners of your Surface
* The case base would provide decent protection

Con's:
* You can not use the case with the attachable Surface Keyboard, so you are limited in using your Surface only as a
tablet.
* The clear back scratches and marks easily. giving it a worn and unclear view of the back of your surface.
* The fold-able cover is not very good protection for your screen, it is relatively thin
* Because the cover is relatively thin, it is not really a stable stand when folded and the tablet is on it

This case does not really live up to the OtterBox brand. It seems quite an inconvenience to not be able to use your Surface keyboard without taking the case off. You would be limited in only being able to use your Surface as a Tablet. For some this maybe acceptable. But for my wife who travels extensively and uses her Surface more than her desktop for work, that just is not feasible. Plus, having to buy additional protection for your screen is also a negative aspect. I just would not trust this cover alone to keep the screen safe from breakage.

Overall, my wife will not be using this case on her Surface.
text_fidelity_b: OTTERBOX SYMMETRY FOLIO SERIES Case for Microsoft Surface Pro 7 - Retail Packaging - STARRY NIGHT (CLEAR/BLACK/BLACK PU/DARK GREY MICROSUED)

text_fidelity_a:
Regetek 7" Double DIN Touchscreen in Dash Bluetooth Car Stereo Mp3 Audio 1080P Video Player FM Radio/AM Radio/TF/USB/AUX-in + Remote Control I received this as a free review sample. The reason why I subtracted a star is the cables (both the one from the charger to the control module, and the 3.5mm connection) are hardwired. This means that if either cable becomes damaged it can cost more to repair than to replace, unless you have the skills to repair them. Had the charger been configured with a micro USB port and the control module with a 3.5mm port for separate cables that can be easily purchased just about anywhere (including pharmacies and supermarkets these days), a damaged cable would be an easy swap and the value and utility of this solution been a lot more.

Operationally, this kit functions as promised. The mic will pass through commands if your phone has voice recognition, and the overall quality of sound is more a function of your vehicle's stereo system than this unit. Since my vehicle is already bluetooth-enabled I used a small, powered speaker with a 3.5mm input to test this. Since the cable, as mentioned, is fixed I had to still perform the test in my vehicle. The sound quality was overall good, and making and receiving test calls were easy and the connections clear enough to be heard without 'can you hear me now?'

Surprisingly the extra USB port in the charger was relatively fast, and proved to be as good as any high-speed (but non QC) charger on both my Note 4 and a friend's iPhone 5S. In fact, that is why I only subtracted one star because while the cable issue does detract, the charging capability of the extra port is better than I expected.

Bottom line: this is an OK hand's free solution for older vehicles that have an AUX port, but no bluetooth (and you NEED an AUX port to make this work.) Since the control module is hardwired into a lighter-style charger you cannot use this with a home stereo that does not have bluetooth, but does have 3.5mm input. There are similar solutions that use basically the same design, but replaceable cables that do allow this, so this one is restricted to vehicle-only use. If that is all you need, this one does perform as claimed.
text_fidelity_b: Regetek 7" Double DIN Touchscreen in Dash Bluetooth Car Stereo Mp3 Audio 1080P Video Player FM Radio/AM Radio/TF/USB/AUX-in + Remote Control

text_fidelity_a:
Leather Laptop Messenger Bag for Men - Handmade Laptop Briefcase Satchel by Leather Centric This LEATHER LAPTOP MESSENGER BAG FOR MEN (by Leather Centric) is made of real leather--animal hide, NOT the man-made “pleather” stuff that’s often marketed on Amazon as “real leather” or “genuine leather”. That’s a big plus, but the bag itself has a lot of minuses.

First, the bag’s styling is so old-fashioned, it makes the bag look cheap. You have to really love the 1950s “retro” look, to like the overall appearance. The bag definitely looks handmade, but it also looks crudely rustic.

Second, although the bag has lots of zippered compartments (inside and outside), it is only 3” deep. It has no expansion gussets, so the total capacity is one laptop or one very thick sheaf of documents. Internal zipper compartments are relatively useless if a bag can’t expand to hold the things added to the compartments.

Third, the bag is difficult to open. It opens with two metal clasps--these are hidden beneath the purely decorative buckled front straps. You have to pull up on both clasps at once to lift the flap, and you can’t do this easily without laying the bag flat on one side, or holding it on your lap. The leather flap itself is very stiff (at least when the bag is new), and this adds to the opening difficulty.

Fourth, the bag has no locking mechanism. Not that it is easy to open (see previous paragraph).

Fifth, the brass fittings must tarnish very easily, because the bag arrives with every single exposed brass piece wrapped tightly in thin plastic wrap. It takes something very sharp to cut the plastic, and you must be careful not to scratch the fittings. (I succeeded in removing the wrappings without damaging the bag, but I punctured my left wrist with an Olfa knife in the process.)

The bag is reasonably priced (about $90 on Amazon). It comes with a snap-on shoulder carrying strap, and has a sturdy, permanently attached satchel handle. The handle is very comfortable. The bag leather is already distressed, so you needn’t worry about scratches. This is a truly rugged laptop bag.
text_fidelity_b: Leather Laptop Messenger Bag for Men - Handmade Laptop Briefcase Satchel by Leather Centric

Garmin nüvi 255W 4.3-Inch Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I bought this as a graduation present for my nephew and, of course, had to try it out for a while just to make sure it was "in proper functioning order." (OK, so I like toys even more than the kids do).

Very nice system! It's a nice improvement from earlier Nuvi's I've used. Love the improved software, especially the full-time next-turn indicator (long a favorite feature of mine on Magellan units). The screen layout is attractive and easy to use, even for those of us with less than perfect eyesight.

While I personally like the Magellan systems better for my own use, I picked this for the nephew for a couple of reasons. First, it has features such as the ability to download Google maps directions. Not something I would use, but a nice feature for those who would use it. Second, it has the ability to display the speed limit. While it won't prevent speeding, at least it's a reminder for a younger driver to keep it slow.

I found the routing engine to be top-notch. Every GPS does that a bit different, but every route I planned on it was plotted out in a logical manner. It's a bit slower to detect off-route conditions and re-route compared with Magellans, but certainly does it at an acceptable speed. Boot up and acquitiion time is very good, as it the overall build quality and form factor.

A good option to pick up is a bean bag mount such as a NavMat. Makes it far easier to hide the GPS without any trace to tip off potential theves.

Most important, it has Garmin support - they are far better than Magellan, and can be used as a resource for someone who is using their first GPS. I was sorry to have to hand it back over the the nephew, but he's thrilled with it!
text_fidelity_b: Garmin nüvi 255W 4.3-Inch Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Microsoft Wireless Rechargeable Laser Mouse 7000 Mac/Windows I have mixed feelings about this mouse. On one hand it is a pleasure to use. On the other, charging it leaves much to be desired.

This is a fairly large mouse, sculpted nicely to fit most peoples' hands. I have large hands and I have found this mouse to be a good fit. It is comfortable to grip, the scroll wheel is smooth and easy to turn, and the buttons are easy to press without being hyper-sensitive. Ergonomics are this mouse's strongest attribute.

In use, the mouse is on par with other Microsoft mice I have used. It is accurate. Unlike some of the comments by other reviewers here, I have had no issue with it being too sensitive or too precise. The performance has, in my opinion, been average. This is not a bad thing - Microsoft mice are usually very consistent and this one fits the norm.

Where I ran into difficulty with this mouse was in charging it. I read a lot of other reviews on this mouse beforehand so I was prepared for issues with charging. That said, I was still having issues getting the mouse to charge the battery until I cut part of a 3x5 index card, folded it up and crammed it into the battery compartment with the battery. There have been enough other people that have had to do similarly odd things to rule out the possibility of this being an isolated case.

The battery can be put into a normal charger, but that defeats the purpose.

This is not a bad mouse. It's actually quite good and I would recommend it except for the recharging issue. As a wireless mouse it is fine, but as a recharging mouse it needs a design revisit.

text_fidelity_a:
RCA RD1006 Discwasher D4+ Vinyl Record Care System This is the best record cleaning I tried so far. I is very effective in removing dust (and associated static noise) from records that are in reasonably good shape. Of course, it cannot repair records which have been damaged due to being played while dirty. If you acquire a used record in dirty condition, it is probably a good idea to wash it with distilled water first before using the discwasher on it.

I noticed that there are several one-star reviews complaining about the direction of fibers on the cleaning pad that comes with this system. Yes, the cords of the corduroy-like microfiber material does run along the edge of the brush, but this is actually how it should be to provide even coverage across all the grooves. The cords of any fabric is much too thick to fit into the actual grooves on the record. If the cords were to run along the direction of the the grooves, some grooves would be cleaned and some wouldn't. Having the cords being perpendicular to the grooves on the record ensures that all grooves get cleaned evenly. After all, it is the microfibers, not the cords of the fabric, doing the cleaning.

Another advantage of cords running perpendicular to the grooves of the record is that, as you slowly rotate the brush on its axis (as shown in the provided directions), dust that has been collected gets trapped between the cords that are being lifted off the record as the next (clean) cord of the fabric starts making contact with the record surface.
text_fidelity_b: RCA RD1006 Discwasher D4+ Vinyl Record Care System

text_fidelity_a:
Microsoft Surface Book 13.5" (Intel Core i5, 8GB RAM, 256 GB) We have a number of surface tablets in our house, and this was my first surface book. I got it hoping for some increased performance for using with my landscape CAD program, and I did notice a difference in the smoothness when working with CAD on this device as opposed to my other comparable surface tablets. The better performance only works when it is hooked up to the keyboard, which is fine for CAD work.

I also like to use this as a tablet for photo editing work related to my business, and here I noticed my number one complaint about this device, which is that the tablet part itself does not have the little foldout stand that all of the other surface tablets have. I guess they think that you will just connect it to the keyboard, but sometimes I want it to be as flexible and lightweight as a regular surface Pro tablet, and while you can unhook it from the keyboard and use it as a tablet, it feels more bulky and the lack of stand makes it less flexible in its use than the surface Pro tablets.

One thing I did notice is that you can connect it to the keyboard backwards and use the keyboard as a stand that way, however that does not bend to the same angle as the tablet stands do on a regular surface Pro.

I also think that the battery life is a lot less on this one than on the surface Pro tablets. Even when not connected to the keyboard and the increased computing performance that you get from that, it seems to wear down its batteries on tablet mode in about 30 to 45 minutes of photo editing. When I worked on my surface tablet in this fashion, I feel like I got a little less than two hours before having to recharge.

Overall, if you plan to use this primarily plugged in as a laptop and only occasionally as a tablet, the increased performance from the attached keyboard make this a worthwhile choice if you do gaming or more high-powered computing. However, if you are primarily using it as a tablet or in places where battery life is a critical consideration, I would suggest the regular surface Pro tablet instead.

In terms of accessories, I use the surface pen constantly, but haven't reached for the other accessories much at all. The surface pen makes it so smooth to make notes on photographs to convey ideas to people, and is great for photo editing.
text_fidelity_b: Microsoft Surface Book 13.5" (Intel Core i5, 8GB RAM, 256 GB)

Snugg iPod Nano 7G / 8G Carabina Case (Black Silicone) for iPod Nano (7th/8th Generation) Update - the kindly people at Snugg sent me a new case, frankly, I wasn't real enthused about it, I figured it would probably still have the design flaws that made it a worthless $20 investment, but I was wrong, wrong, wrong. That will show me to stop being such a pessimist. I couldn't be happier with this now, it is everything I was hoping for, it clips on to the strap of my apron when I'm getting my cooking on, it hooks onto my backpack when I'm out riding. All in all, it is wonderful.

The headphone/earbud thingies I use, pretty standard ones called Coby also the ones that came with my ipod are able to make contact with the bottom portal which is now clear of the protective rubber. The carabiner clip seems slightly more substantial, I'd have to weigh it or take it apart somehow to verify this part.

So here's my old review, use this for info, in case you end up with a flawed Snugg, I guess you should just return it then, or maybe the bugs have been worked out now and all new Snuggs are good. Anyways, here's the old review with a listing of the pertinent problems.

!OLD REVIEW!

The problems Other people have mentioned, mainly the difficulty inserting the nano into the clip case, wasn't really a problem for me. After watching my husband struggle with it for a few minutes I pulled it away from him and decided to do it myself. I was aided in this task by two things, 1) I have more fine motor skills than he does and a lot more experience with tiny detail work (painting, beading, etc) and 2) I have fingernails, real ones not acrylic (I think acrylic nails would be too thick).

I used the thin edge of my fingernail to seat the bottom of the nano in the case after sliding it top first under the rubber part at the top of the clip case.

Once it was in my iPod did appear to be very secure. The carabina clip is a bit of an exaggeration, it isn't nearly as sturdy as a carabiner, the like of which is used by climbers, this is more of a jewelry version and feels very lightweight, I'm not pleased with that.

I paid $8 more for the clip aspect of this case and the clip is there but isn't as functional and sturdy as I'd hoped.

The second fail for this case is that the rubber casing covers part of the headphone port.

I bought this case along with my new iPod, so once I'd unpacked both, I loaded a new audiobook onto my new iPod and slipped the case on and decided to take a listen. Nothing.

I couldn't hear anything at all. It was so disappointing. For a moment I thought that my new iPod was defective. Nope.

It turns out that there wasn't enough room for the headphone jack to make a complete connection unless you peeled back the case wall and held it in place while listening.

So annoying.

Anyways, I have a x-acto knife and have been debating whether or not to modify the bottom of the case myself (the clip isn't great and it kinda ticks me off that I have to act as seamstress for this failure of a product if I want to use it). But sending stuff back is tedious and time consuming (okay, it takes about five minutes to return stuff on Amazon, but still, I don't want to do it!).

text_fidelity_a:
iHome 2-In-1 Pen Stylus for iPad/iPad 2 and all Touch Screen Devices (IH-IP2202) I expect that no one is going to use a stylus 100% of the time with their touch screen. There are, however, some times when a stylus is more convenient than using your finger. Drawing objects freehand is a common example. Another example is when you need to precisely move objects around the screen (eg in a CAD program) and this is difficult with your finger because your finger blocks your view of the target area.

There are many many touch screen stylus for sale on Amazon. Some cost less than 50 cents each. All the latest stylus have similar round soft touch rubber tips. All seem to work about the same. This iHome stylus doesn't seem to work any better than the others that I have tried.

The iHome stylus is better looking than most of the competition because of the long slim shape with silver-tone accents. Some of the cheap ones look very plasticy (though they do work just as well). Some other stylus are fatter, which makes them easier to grip if you have large hands.

The built-in ball-point pen is a feature that most other stylus do not have. The pen works well, though I do not know how easy ink refills will be to find. There is no literature in the package about what refills it can use.

Is this product worth $15? I have to say no, but I'm a cheapskate. You can decide on value for yourself, but look at the competition first.
text_fidelity_b: iHome 2-In-1 Pen Stylus for iPad/iPad 2 and all Touch Screen Devices (IH-IP2202)

text_fidelity_a: Ring Video Doorbell Pro – Upgraded, with added security features and a sleek design (existing doorbell wiring required) Our house is set quite far back from the road and is surrounded by trees. We have the motion zones set up so that as soon as a car reaches the cement portion of our driveway it alerts us. It has worked well for us and we don’t get many false alerts. The few we have had were from wasps hovering right in front of it or spiders crawling over it. The motion zones were easy to set up and we like that you can snooze alerts. We have the ring linked to Alexa so she also announces when someone approaches. The only problem with that is even if you have the motion alerts on snooze she will still announce them. This is annoying when someone is outside doing something. The only way to get her to stop announcing for that time is by going into the Alexa app and shutting off motion alerts. Then we have to remember to turn them back on again. It is very dark around our house at night because there are no streetlights and during the summer months we keep outdoor lights off. The night vision on the ring is excellent. We can see images very clearly. We’ve been so impressed with this doorbell that we’re going to buy a second one to put on our other door.
text_fidelity_b: Ring Video Doorbell Pro – Upgraded, with added security features and a sleek design (existing doorbell wiring required)
